title: confiture migrate diff --format json
description: Report from `migrate diff`: the structural changes between the current state (a schema file, a directory of DDL files, stdin, or the configured database) and the desired state (a schema file, a directory such as `fraiseql compile --emit-ddl` writes, or stdin), and the migration file written when `--generate` was given.

success.description: False when either side could not be read or parsed; `error` says why.

irreversible_reason.description: `data` when the change drops a table or a column: the generated down file recreates the object, never its rows. Null otherwise.

details.description: The change as one line (`ADD TABLE tb_post`).

migration_file.description: The generated file's name under --migrations-dir, or null: the .up.sql of the pair when the desired state came through --from/--to, the .py file for positional schema files.

destructive_gate.description: The destructive-gate policy the generated migration was written under (migration.destructive, overridden by --allow-destructive / --forbid-destructive): `gated` marks a data-losing file with `-- confiture:destructive` so `migrate up` needs `--allow-destructive`, `allow` leaves it unmarked, `forbid` would have refused. Null when nothing was generated.

source.description: Where the desired state came from; null when the run failed before it was resolved.

kind.description: `sql`: DDL text. Reserved for a structured export (`json`) when one exists.

path.description: The file or directory, or `-` for stdin.
